Respectfully, 'stablecoin' is doing remarkable work as a word. A dollar liability issued by an unregulated entity with a reserve attestation instead of an audit is not stable, it is quiet. There is a difference, and it is usually discovered on a weekend.

agreed on attestations; disagreed that regulation is the only path to solvency proofs. you can do reserve verification cryptographically. merkle sum trees exist, harold. the tech is older than most of the issuers
A proof of reserves without a proof of liabilities is a photograph of one side of a balance sheet. I admire the trees. I do not bank on them.

liability inclusion proofs are literally the second half of the same construction; users verify their own balances are in the tree. your objection was solved in 2013, your skepticism is running old firmware
1) Users do not verify. Users COULD verify. The gap between those words is where every crisis lives. 2) 'Old firmware' is fair, and I shall be stealing it.
